programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean bho Coats ann am Pàislig, air a lìbhrigeadh le Iain MacFhionghain. Am measg na seinneadairean bidh Amy NicAoidh, Emma NicLeòid agus Seumas Greumach. Cuideachd, an còisir Soisgeul fo stiùir Gareth Fuller. Bidh Dolina NicMhathain a’ meòrachadh air cuspair creideimh le leughadh agus smuain, dàn is seallaidhean spioradail à Tiriodh ann an companachd Dòmhnall Eachann Meek agus bidh seirm adhraidh air a’ phìob aig Chloe Steele à Manachainn nan Lios. Iain MacKinnon presents the spiritual series with a mix of hymns, psalms and readings from Coats in Paisley. Among the singers performing are Amy MacKay, Emma MacLeod and James Graham. Plus the choir Soisgeul conducted by Gareth Fuller. Dolina Matheson reflects on her beliefs with a selected reading and thought, spiritual poetry and landscapes in the company of Donald E Meek in Tiree and Chloe Steele performs a tune of worship on the pipes from Beauly Priory. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Mach à Seo!

programme.title: Coin Trusaidh/Muster Dogs
programme.desc: Air an t-slighe bheòthail seo, tha sinn a’ faighinn sealladh nas dlùithe air beatha còig luchd-trèanaidh bho air feadh Astràilia agus iad uile a’ gabhail pàirt san deuchainn againn: cuilean Kelpie a thoirt gu ìre – airson a bhith mar phàirt de sgioba nan con trusaidh. As t-earrach, tha na cuileanan a-nis ceithir mìosan a dh’aois agus ge bith a bheil iad deiseil no nach eil, thèid iad uile tro na deuchainnean mòra a mheasas ma tha iad air an t-slighe cheart airson a bhith nan coin trusaidh math. An action-packed yet intimate character journey about the lives of five very different Australian dog trainers as they participate in our experiment: to take a new Kelpie pup and transform it from a greenhorn to an efficient working member of the mustering pack. It’s spring and the puppies are four months old and, ready or not, they each step through the milestone assessments that will determine if they are on track to be quality muster dogs. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Voyages of Discovery
programme.desc: Explorer Paul Rose tells the story of the USS Squalus submarine which became stranded on the bottom of the Atlantic in 1939. No-one had ever been saved from a stricken sub beneath the ocean before, but maverick designer Charles Momsen, who had been ignored by the navy top brass, was suddenly called into action to bring up the crew. Rose meets the last living survivor from the sub and one of the men, now 103, who helped save him. The rescue kick-started a whole new era of technology, laying the foundation for modern deep-sea diving.

programme.title: Bill Oddie Goes Wild
programme.desc: On his home patch of Hampstead Heath in London, Bill Oddie reminisces about his past travels in search of the best of British wildlife. We join him as he muses over some of his most memorable moments, and revisit some of his highlights, low points and outtakes from the past three series.

programme.title: Birding with Bill Oddie
programme.desc: In his practical guide to birdwatching and learning about birds, Bill Oddie revisits his childhood birding haunts to discover how they have changed over 50 years. Bill's first encounter with birds was when he was about seven years old. He found a dunnock's nest with five eggs in - he took one, put it in a matchbox and carefully put it in his back pocket. He then forgot about it, and later, when jumping over a log, crushed it. Egg-collecting is no longer legal, but it did teach him a lesson or two - it got him hooked on birds and taught him the value of patience.

programme.title: Bill Oddie's Top Ten Birds
programme.desc: Bill Oddie counts down the UK's ten most beloved and most villainous birds in a definitive, light-hearted guide to our feathered friends and foes. Bill's poll is based on the thousands of letters he has received over the years from members of the public.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: A programme of remarkable debuts, landmark premieres and history-making moments, featuring a Betsy Jolas debut inspired by Shakespeare's Tempest, music from the Spanish National Orchestra, both recorded this season, soprano Angel Blue's triumphant proms debut, and the first accordion soloist to grace the Last Night of the Proms stage - Ksenija Sidorova - transports us to the streets of Buenos Aires with her rendition of Piazzolla's Libertango.

programme.title: ArtWorks Scotland
programme.desc: Hard-hitting play, based on interviews with former soldiers, that combines words, music and song to deliver a frank and unvarnished account of a Scottish regiment serving in the Iraq war. The National Theatre of Scotland's award-winning production was filmed live in Dingwall.

programme.title: ArtWorks Scotland
programme.desc: An insight by Artworks Scotland into the genesis of Black Watch, the National Theatre of Scotland's portrayal of the Iraq War using eyewitness testimony, news reports and regimental song, first performed at the 2006 Edinburgh Festival.

programme.title: Jane Austen: The Unseen Portrait?
programme.desc: Jane Austen is one of the most celebrated writers of all time, but apart from a rough sketch by her sister Cassandra, we have very little idea what she looked like. Biographer Dr Paula Byrne thinks that is about to change. She believes she has come across a possible portrait of the author, lost to the world for nearly two centuries. Can the picture stand up to forensic analysis and scrutiny by art historians and world-leading Austen experts? How might it change our image of the author? And what might the portrait reveal about Jane Austen and her world? Martha Kearney seeks answers as she follows Dr Byrne on her quest.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles saddles up for a gallop around an antiques fair in Kent, as he visits a museum in Maidstone that’s home to a unique collection of horse-drawn vehicles and transport-related treasures. The collection is the legacy of former local businessman Sir Garrard Tyrwhitt-Drake, who began collecting carriages when he saw that the motor car was forcing the horse-drawn vehicles of his childhood off the road. Over at the fair in Detling, two teams of families are under starter’s orders, with experts Catherine Southon and Mark Stacey by their side. On the red team are father and daughter Hash and Jaymeesha, and on the blues are mum and son Jenny and Dan. The reds have a few tricks up their sleeves when Hash performs a card trick for a stallholder to get a discount on the ticket price! Meanwhile, the blues aren’t cock-a-hoop when they learn the price of a French bronzed rooster. Then it’s off to the auction in Portsmouth, where John Cameron gives Eric the lowdown on the teams’ lots and auctioneer Daniel Tricker does the business on the rostrum.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Adam Henson meets young farmers navigating the challenges and rewards of producing our food. This week, he’s in Cumbria with 27-year-old farmer Georgia Hunter and her flock of goats, which she keeps in partnership with her dad. Whilst helping milk the flock, Adam finds out how the family turned to keeping goats after a bad lambing season. Following a series of setbacks, Georgia and her dad decided to turn their fortunes around by producing their own goat's cheese and soap. Adam learns that Georgia, because of her experiences, is now an advocate for mental health support in the local farming community. Adam also looks back through the Countryfile archives, revisiting some of the inspirational farmers we have met from across the UK.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of Brodie Castle in northern Scotland, home to the Brodie Clan since the 16th century. Fiona Bruce explores the castle and its treasures, including a dog portrait by Edwin Landseer that was cut out of a larger canvas, and in the Playful Garden she meets a giant rabbit. Silver specialist Gordon Foster discovers a beautiful silver trophy from a local curling club that dates to 1896, while ceramics expert Steven Moore gets to reunite Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan in the form of novelty teapots inspired by the satirical TV show Spitting Image. Three members of an extended family are brought together for the very first time when expert Adam Schoon examines a selection of items that belonged to a shared ancestor, Scottish footballing legend Robert Boyd. Mark Smith is fascinated to see the contents of a large footlocker that belonged to a Scotsman who enlisted in the American army during the First World War, while Judith Miller challenges Fiona to put three carved wooden ‘treen’ objects in order of value.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The European Athletics Championships draw to a close in Birmingham with the final night of action on the track and in the field at the Alexander Stadium. Global superstar Mondo Duplantis tops the billing in the men’s pole vault, with the fastest woman in Europe over 1,500m, Georgia Hunter Bell, aiming for her first senior outdoor title. There are also three relay golds on offer, including, for the first time at the championships, the mixed sprint relay. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio for the last time by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe on commentary duty.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles saddles up for a gallop around an antiques fair in Kent, as he visits a museum in Maidstone that’s home to a unique collection of horse-drawn vehicles and transport-related treasures. The collection is the legacy of former local businessman Sir Garrard Tyrwhitt-Drake, who began collecting carriages when he saw that the motor car was forcing the horse-drawn vehicles of his childhood off the road. Over at the fair in Detling, two teams of families are under starter’s orders, with experts Catherine Southon and Mark Stacey by their side. On the red team are father and daughter Hash and Jaymeesha, and on the blues are mum and son Jenny and Dan. The reds have a few tricks up their sleeves when Hash performs a card trick for a stallholder to get a discount on the ticket price! Meanwhile, the blues aren’t cock-a-hoop when they learn the price of a French bronzed rooster. Then it’s off to the auction in Portsmouth, where John Cameron gives Eric the lowdown on the teams’ lots and auctioneer Daniel Tricker does the business on the rostrum.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of Brodie Castle in northern Scotland, home to the Brodie Clan since the 16th century. Fiona Bruce explores the castle and its treasures, including a dog portrait by Edwin Landseer that was cut out of a larger canvas, and in the Playful Garden she meets a giant rabbit. Silver specialist Gordon Foster discovers a beautiful silver trophy from a local curling club that dates to 1896, while ceramics expert Steven Moore gets to reunite Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan in the form of novelty teapots inspired by the satirical TV show Spitting Image. Three members of an extended family are brought together for the very first time when expert Adam Schoon examines a selection of items that belonged to a shared ancestor, Scottish footballing legend Robert Boyd. Mark Smith is fascinated to see the contents of a large footlocker that belonged to a Scotsman who enlisted in the American army during the First World War, while Judith Miller challenges Fiona to put three carved wooden ‘treen’ objects in order of value.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The European Athletics Championships draw to a close in Birmingham with the final night of action on the track and in the field at the Alexander Stadium. Global superstar Mondo Duplantis tops the billing in the men’s pole vault, with the fastest woman in Europe over 1,500m, Georgia Hunter Bell, aiming for her first senior outdoor title. There are also three relay golds on offer, including, for the first time at the championships, the mixed sprint relay. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio for the last time by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe on commentary duty.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles saddles up for a gallop around an antiques fair in Kent, as he visits a museum in Maidstone that’s home to a unique collection of horse-drawn vehicles and transport-related treasures. The collection is the legacy of former local businessman Sir Garrard Tyrwhitt-Drake, who began collecting carriages when he saw that the motor car was forcing the horse-drawn vehicles of his childhood off the road. Over at the fair in Detling, two teams of families are under starter’s orders, with experts Catherine Southon and Mark Stacey by their side. On the red team are father and daughter Hash and Jaymeesha, and on the blues are mum and son Jenny and Dan. The reds have a few tricks up their sleeves when Hash performs a card trick for a stallholder to get a discount on the ticket price! Meanwhile, the blues aren’t cock-a-hoop when they learn the price of a French bronzed rooster. Then it’s off to the auction in Portsmouth, where John Cameron gives Eric the lowdown on the teams’ lots and auctioneer Daniel Tricker does the business on the rostrum.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Adam Henson meets young farmers navigating the challenges and rewards of producing our food. This week, he’s in Cumbria with 27-year-old farmer Georgia Hunter and her flock of goats, which she keeps in partnership with her dad. Whilst helping milk the flock, Adam finds out how the family turned to keeping goats after a bad lambing season. Following a series of setbacks, Georgia and her dad decided to turn their fortunes around by producing their own goat's cheese and soap. Adam learns that Georgia, because of her experiences, is now an advocate for mental health support in the local farming community. Adam also looks back through the Countryfile archives, revisiting some of the inspirational farmers we have met from across the UK.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of Brodie Castle in northern Scotland, home to the Brodie Clan since the 16th century. Fiona Bruce explores the castle and its treasures, including a dog portrait by Edwin Landseer that was cut out of a larger canvas, and in the Playful Garden she meets a giant rabbit. Silver specialist Gordon Foster discovers a beautiful silver trophy from a local curling club that dates to 1896, while ceramics expert Steven Moore gets to reunite Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan in the form of novelty teapots inspired by the satirical TV show Spitting Image. Three members of an extended family are brought together for the very first time when expert Adam Schoon examines a selection of items that belonged to a shared ancestor, Scottish footballing legend Robert Boyd. Mark Smith is fascinated to see the contents of a large footlocker that belonged to a Scotsman who enlisted in the American army during the First World War, while Judith Miller challenges Fiona to put three carved wooden ‘treen’ objects in order of value.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The European Athletics Championships draw to a close in Birmingham with the final night of action on the track and in the field at the Alexander Stadium. Global superstar Mondo Duplantis tops the billing in the men’s pole vault, with the fastest woman in Europe over 1,500m, Georgia Hunter Bell, aiming for her first senior outdoor title. There are also three relay golds on offer, including, for the first time at the championships, the mixed sprint relay. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio for the last time by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe on commentary duty.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles saddles up for a gallop around an antiques fair in Kent, as he visits a museum in Maidstone that’s home to a unique collection of horse-drawn vehicles and transport-related treasures. The collection is the legacy of former local businessman Sir Garrard Tyrwhitt-Drake, who began collecting carriages when he saw that the motor car was forcing the horse-drawn vehicles of his childhood off the road. Over at the fair in Detling, two teams of families are under starter’s orders, with experts Catherine Southon and Mark Stacey by their side. On the red team are father and daughter Hash and Jaymeesha, and on the blues are mum and son Jenny and Dan. The reds have a few tricks up their sleeves when Hash performs a card trick for a stallholder to get a discount on the ticket price! Meanwhile, the blues aren’t cock-a-hoop when they learn the price of a French bronzed rooster. Then it’s off to the auction in Portsmouth, where John Cameron gives Eric the lowdown on the teams’ lots and auctioneer Daniel Tricker does the business on the rostrum.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles saddles up for a gallop around an antiques fair in Kent, as he visits a museum in Maidstone that’s home to a unique collection of horse-drawn vehicles and transport-related treasures. The collection is the legacy of former local businessman Sir Garrard Tyrwhitt-Drake, who began collecting carriages when he saw that the motor car was forcing the horse-drawn vehicles of his childhood off the road. Over at the fair in Detling, two teams of families are under starter’s orders, with experts Catherine Southon and Mark Stacey by their side. On the red team are father and daughter Hash and Jaymeesha, and on the blues are mum and son Jenny and Dan. programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Adam Henson meets young farmers navigating the challenges and rewards of producing our food. This week, he’s in Cumbria with 27-year-old farmer Georgia Hunter and her flock of goats, which she keeps in partnership with her dad. Whilst helping milk the flock, Adam finds out how the family turned to keeping goats after a bad lambing season. Following a series of setbacks, Georgia and her dad decided to turn their fortunes around by producing their own goat's cheese and soap. Adam learns that Georgia, because of her experiences, is now an advocate for mental health support in the local farming community. Adam also looks back through the Countryfile archives, revisiting some of the inspirational farmers we have met from across the UK.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of Brodie Castle in northern Scotland, home to the Brodie Clan since the 16th century. Fiona Bruce explores the castle and its treasures, including a dog portrait by Edwin Landseer that was cut out of a larger canvas, and in the Playful Garden she meets a giant rabbit. Silver specialist Gordon Foster discovers a beautiful silver trophy from a local curling club that dates to 1896, while ceramics expert Steven Moore gets to reunite Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan in the form of novelty teapots inspired by the satirical TV show Spitting Image. Three members of an extended family are brought together for the very first time when expert Adam Schoon examines a selection of items that belonged to a shared ancestor, Scottish footballing legend Robert Boyd. Mark Smith is fascinated to see the contents of a large footlocker that belonged to a Scotsman who enlisted in the American army during the First World War, while Judith Miller challenges Fiona to put three carved wooden ‘treen’ objects in order of value.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The European Athletics Championships draw to a close in Birmingham with the final night of action on the track and in the field at the Alexander Stadium. Global superstar Mondo Duplantis tops the billing in the men’s pole vault, with the fastest woman in Europe over 1,500m, Georgia Hunter Bell, aiming for her first senior outdoor title. There are also three relay golds on offer, including, for the first time at the championships, the mixed sprint relay. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio for the last time by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe on commentary duty.

programme.desc: Adam Henson meets young farmers navigating the challenges and rewards of producing our food. This week, he’s in Cumbria with 27-year-old farmer Georgia Hunter and her flock of goats, which she keeps in partnership with her dad. Whilst helping milk the flock, Adam finds out how the family turned to keeping goats after a bad lambing season. Following a series of setbacks, Georgia and her dad decided to turn their fortunes around by producing their own goat's cheese and soap. Adam learns that Georgia, because of her experiences, is now an advocate for mental health support in the local farming community. Adam also looks back through the Countryfile archives, revisiting some of the inspirational farmers we have met from across the UK.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow comes from the beautiful grounds of Brodie Castle in northern Scotland, home to the Brodie Clan since the 16th century. Fiona Bruce explores the castle and its treasures, including a dog portrait by Edwin Landseer that was cut out of a larger canvas, and in the Playful Garden she meets a giant rabbit. Silver specialist Gordon Foster discovers a beautiful silver trophy from a local curling club that dates to 1896, while ceramics expert Steven Moore gets to reunite Margaret Thatcher and Ronald Reagan in the form of novelty teapots inspired by the satirical TV show Spitting Image. Three members of an extended family are brought together for the very first time when expert Adam Schoon examines a selection of items that belonged to a shared ancestor, Scottish footballing legend Robert Boyd. Mark Smith is fascinated to see the contents of a large footlocker that belonged to a Scotsman who enlisted in the American army during the First World War, while Judith Miller challenges Fiona to put three carved wooden ‘treen’ objects in order of value.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The European Athletics Championships draw to a close in Birmingham with the final night of action on the track and in the field at the Alexander Stadium. Global superstar Mondo Duplantis tops the billing in the men’s pole vault, with the fastest woman in Europe over 1,500m, Georgia Hunter Bell, aiming for her first senior outdoor title. There are also three relay golds on offer, including, for the first time at the championships, the mixed sprint relay. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio for the last time by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe on commentary duty.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles saddles up for a gallop around an antiques fair in Kent, as he visits a museum in Maidstone that’s home to a unique collection of horse-drawn vehicles and transport-related treasures. The collection is the legacy of former local businessman Sir Garrard Tyrwhitt-Drake, who began collecting carriages when he saw that the motor car was forcing the horse-drawn vehicles of his childhood off the road. Over at the fair in Detling, two teams of families are under starter’s orders, with experts Catherine Southon and Mark Stacey by their side. On the red team are father and daughter Hash and Jaymeesha, and on the blues are mum and son Jenny and Dan. The reds have a few tricks up their sleeves when Hash performs a card trick for a stallholder to get a discount on the ticket price! Meanwhile, the blues aren’t cock-a-hoop when they learn the price of a French bronzed rooster. Then it’s off to the auction in Portsmouth, where John Cameron gives Eric the lowdown on the teams’ lots and auctioneer Daniel Tricker does the business on the rostrum.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: All the weekend national, UK-wide and international news on Sunday evening at 7.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Dom and Rich join local craftsmen in a race to restore a memorial sculpture that has been scarred by decades of coastal weather before a poignant remembrance service for lives lost at sea. In Kincardine, Will collects Lyndsey’s unusual family heirloom – a cast-iron pan that cooked thousands of meals – hoping electrolysis will transform it from garden gate stop to a camping essential, before heading to the Borders to learn from some celebrated rush-seated chair makers.

programme.title: Island Crossings
programme.desc: Kerrera Island’s annual triathlon is at risk due to bad weather, while a folk legend explains why being a binman on Barra makes him proud.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: John and Craig of the Special Operations Response Team are called to Glasgow city centre, where a public brawl has broken out on a busy Saturday evening. At the scene, John helps to coordinate the ambulance response, engaging with police to help keep the two factions separate. Meanwhile, Craig treats someone who was caught up in the melee. The next morning, ambulance crew Jim and Kire are called to a church in the south of the city. The patient is Ian, a member of the congregation who has collapsed complaining of chest pain. When the team get Ian into the back of their ambulance, they carry out an ECG of his heart, which gives some concerning readings. Thirty miles away in Livingston, ambulance crew Aaron and Alex are called to see George, who has been found on the pavement close to his home after struggling with his speech and mobility for the past year. Although George hasn’t been injured in the fall, the team need to make sure he is safe to be left on his own. However, their concerns for George and his wife, Susan, grow when they take him home.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Sitcom featuring Jack and Victor, two irrepressible pensioners first seen in the comedy series Chewin' the Fat, along with their dependable pals Winston and Tam, fresh out of Craiglang and taking on the world. Jack and Victor decide they can't take it with them, so they decide to spend their funeral fund on life's little luxuries. Meanwhile golfers Tam and Winston get involved in a foursome with a gang of neds.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Another shift at the coalface of crime-fighting for the lads and lassies of the Scottish Police Force. Showing no fear whatsoever, they jump in an elevator to battle claustrophobia, compare myth v reality to address vigilantism and rake about a hedge to rescue some very public pornography. Plus magic happens at the traffic lights when road cops Singh and McKirdy pull over a couple of Scotland's most celebrated children's entertainers. Comedy fly-on-the-wall documentary starring Jack Docherty, M L Stone and James Allenby-Kirk. With special guest stars Artie and Cilla from the Singing Kettle.

programme.title: Edinburgh Unlocked
programme.desc: Unlock the best of the Edinburgh Festival with award-winning comedian Mark Nelson, bringing you the best comedy, music, cabaret and theatre from all over the world. Mark and his all-star team of reporters have scoured the brochures to find you the funniest, wildest and weirdest shows from the capital in this month-long extravaganza of chaos.

programme.title: Style Fixers
programme.desc: Jamie helps Muskaan realise her influencer-chic fantasy, and Alannah transforms Alannah-Jayne’s style to reflect her life as a busy professional mum. With some star finds in the charity shops and creative upcycles, including Jamie’s version of a £750 designer shoe, both Style Fixers are giving it their all - but who will win when their clients rate them at the end?

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Adam Henson is in West Sussex with 26-year-old soft fruit grower Archie Evans, who took over the family business determined to put his own stamp on it. As they bring in the harvest, Archie explains why he scaled back production, moved away from supplying major supermarkets and began selling directly to customers. With the family’s finances at stake, will his gamble secure the farm’s future? Adam also delves into the Countryfile archives to revisit some of the inspirational farmers we have met across the UK.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection
programme.desc: Glasgow Central Mosque, Scotland’s first purpose-built mosque, welcomes us for Jummah, the weekly congregational prayer in Islam which takes place every Friday in the early afternoon. The service replaces the zuhr prayer, one of the five daily prayers of Islam. Jummah is central to Islamic worship and a reminder of faith, unity and a moment of reflection. The service will be led by the mosque’s senior imam, Maulana Abdul Ghafoor, and attended by more than 2,000 worshippers from the Glasgow Muslim community. The Jummah prayer will begin with the Adhan (the call to prayer) recited by one of the mosque’s students. The imam will then deliver the khutba, or Friday sermon, before leading the congregation in prayer, in which he will recite three chapters from the Qur'an, beginning with the opening chapter, Surah Al-Fatiha.

programme.title: Top Hat
programme.desc: In the quintessential Astaire and Rogers musical, an American dancer staying at a hotel in London falls in love with the guest staying in the room below. However, she gets her wires crossed, convinces herself that the dancer is already hitched and hotfoots it off to Venice. Classic numbers include Cheek to Cheek and Top Hat. This is Fred and Ginger's fourth pairing, but the first with a screenplay written specifically for them.

programme.title: The Best Dishes Ever
programme.desc: Ainsley Harriott introduces a selection of classic recipes from some of the BBC's best-loved television chefs. This episode features dishes that are great to turn to when time is tight - and it's speed, not vanilla, that is of the essence. The menu includes Nigella Lawson's sausage meatballs, Nigel Slater's herb butter squid, James Martin's icebox cake, the Hairy Bikers' Welsh rarebit and Mary Berry's rich chocolate tray bake with feathered icing.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It's week 5, and the sewers are tackling the wide world of sport. In the Pattern Challenge, they hit the beach to create classic men’s swimming shorts. The Transformation Challenge sees yet another Sewing Bee first, as the remaining eight sewers are divided into pairs for the first ever team challenge: working together to create outfits from recycled windsurf sails. Finally, the sewers are aiming for a strike as they use free-motion embroidery and applique to personalise their made-to-measure bowling shirts.

programme.title: Superman IV - The Quest for Peace
programme.desc: As the Daily Planet is taken over by a tycoon, Lex Luthor steals a strand of Superman's hair and partners with arms dealers to create Nuclear Man, a superhuman entity, to challenge the world order.

programme.title: James Martin's American Adventure
programme.desc: James's American adventure reaches Dallas with a trip to Southfork, the ranch made famous in the world-renowned TV series Dallas - while in town, James visits the location of the Texas State Fair and shares his own pastiche of the TV drama.

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Alan is joined at Manor Farm by Dame Eileen Aitkins who talks about her incredible life both on and off screen. Corrie legend William Roache reveals his secrets to a happy life. Plus, the Queen's eldest grandson Peter Phillips invites us to the sporting event of the summer. We also look at the best in drought-resistant plants, and meet a couple of rare breed Guernsey goats.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: For the last time in this series, Fern is back at The Grove Vets to see how they provide treatment and care to their fluffy patients. Andy performs surgery on pooch Pixie's tummy to remove a worrying tumour. Amy investigates a cat's missing kidney via ultrasound, while James removes an infected wart from geriatric Springerdoodle, Coco. Lottie makes an emergency trip to the clinic after accidentally eating some grapes, and two-year-old feline Nico is back for some X-rays on his leg following surgery last year. And we meet the pets and volunteers taking part in a foster care scheme run by Bristol Animal Rescue Centre.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Chef Tom Kerridge is on the road in Italy's mountains, meeting producers who are just as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck, he discovers the secrets behind chestnuts and pasta. In Emilia-Romagna, he heads high into the Apennines to join local producer Adrian at the chestnut harvest. He learns about their importance to the food of this region, as well as seeing the back-breaking work that goes into harvesting on the side of a mountain. Tom cooks a feast to say thank you: a mouth-watering pork loin steak with chestnuts and wild mushrooms. High in the dramatic Dolomites, Tom visits a desmontegada - a festival to mark the changing of the seasons - where he learns about the powerful impact the fresh mountains have on the local cuisine, including the local pasta. With the mountains as inspiration, he cooks up creamy cheese, sage and pancetta pasta.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S]

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. Our coasts have always been an extreme environment to raise a family, but the challenges of parenthood are exacerbated with warming seas - forming earlier than ever before, a hurricane catches a flamingo colony while their chicks are still on the nest. Rain, wind and rising sea levels are a triple threat, but these extraordinary birds have begun to adapt to the new extremes by extending their breeding window and given those who lost their chicks a second chance - meanwhile, a sea otter mum faces a huge winter storm in California and a clownfish on the Great Barrier Reef witnesses her anemone home bleach. However, the clownfish is not ready to give up and sets about reviving it - perhaps most remarkable of all, though, is a little anole lizard that clings on for dear life during a hurricane, surviving as those with the longest toes are the species most able to keep their grip.

programme.title: Octopussy
programme.desc: The 13th entry in the James Bond film series. 007 is asked to investigate the murder of a fellow agent who was clutching a priceless Faberge egg at the time of his death - the trail leads to the mysterious Octopussy, whose travelling circus features a company of gorgeous and athletic women. Bond and Octopussy share a passionate attraction, but 007 soon discovers that the elegant exiled Afghan prince Kamal Khan is working with a mad Soviet officer to hurl mankind into World War III. As Bond tries to stop the nightmarish scheme, his exploits include a tense chase through the streets of India, a deadly brawl on top of a speeding train, and a treacherous mid-air knife fight on an airplane wing.

programme.title: The Chase Celebrity Special
programme.desc: Bradley Walsh hosts as Raj Bisram, Danielle Harold, John Conteh and Roger Black take on a Chaser to try to win thousands of pounds for their chosen charities.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip. Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Zurich to take on The Governess and The Dark Destroyer, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the final city, lose and it's the first flight home. The episode begins with a quiz on Lake Zurich. An eventful race sees the teams take on games in the city involving Einstein, the FIFA Museum and a chocolate factory, before a journey into the Alps for a cable car quiz at the top of a mountain and a James Bond villain's lair.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Cold-adapted animals are struggling in a warming world - high in the peaks of the Indian Himalayas, a snow leopard is forced from his home by a rival male and embarks on a journey lower into the valley where he encounters the human world. Elsewhere, an arctic ground squirrel in Alaska undertakes the coldest migration of any mammal - to do so, he shuts down many of his biological processes. When he awakes, the squirrel must go through puberty again before finding a mate who is only receptive for a single day - the problem is that the warm weather has brought her out a week early and, despite the intention, he is not equipped to mate. Unless they can adapt quickly, their whole species is under threat - meanwhile, a young arctic fox in Svalbard must face her first winter alone and cross more than 2000 miles of semi-frozen ocean to find polar bears on the sea ice there.

programme.title: Van der Valk

programme.title: Sunny Nights
programme.desc: The first episode of a comedy-drama series. American siblings Martin and Vicki Marvin have flown across the world with dreams of making their burgeoning spray tan company Tansform a success - it's the fresh start they both desperately need, as Martin hopes that building a successful company is the kind of daring gesture that will win back his estranged wife Joyce while Vicki wants to prove that she can be more than just an impulse-driven underachiever. Arriving in Sydney for a beauty convention, the siblings check into the extremely dodgy-looking Sunny Nights motel and quickly get to work trying to find a retail partner who will stock their spray tan - their plans are disrupted when Martin is rejected by Joyce and is led into a drunken one-night stand with Susi Kamdani, who just happens to be a conwoman. The next morning sees footage of the tryst used by criminal Kash Monroe to blackmail Martin - told he needs to pay to keep the footage private, Martin and Vicki must find ten grand.

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Alan is joined at Manor Farm by Dame Eileen Aitkins who talks about her incredible life both on and off screen. Corrie legend William Roache reveals his secrets to a happy life. Plus, the Queen's eldest grandson Peter Phillips invites us to the sporting event of the summer. We also look at the best in drought-resistant plants, and meet a couple of rare breed Guernsey goats.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: For the last time in this series, Fern is back at The Grove Vets to see how they provide treatment and care to their fluffy patients. Andy performs surgery on pooch Pixie's tummy to remove a worrying tumour. Amy investigates a cat's missing kidney via ultrasound, while James removes an infected wart from geriatric Springerdoodle, Coco. Lottie makes an emergency trip to the clinic after accidentally eating some grapes, and two-year-old feline Nico is back for some X-rays on his leg following surgery last year. And we meet the pets and volunteers taking part in a foster care scheme run by Bristol Animal Rescue Centre.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Chef Tom Kerridge is on the road in Italy's mountains, meeting producers who are just as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck, he discovers the secrets behind chestnuts and pasta. In Emilia-Romagna, he heads high into the Apennines to join local producer Adrian at the chestnut harvest. He learns about their importance to the food of this region, as well as seeing the back-breaking work that goes into harvesting on the side of a mountain. Tom cooks a feast to say thank you: a mouth-watering pork loin steak with chestnuts and wild mushrooms. High in the dramatic Dolomites, Tom visits a desmontegada - a festival to mark the changing of the seasons - where he learns about the powerful impact the fresh mountains have on the local cuisine, including the local pasta. With the mountains as inspiration, he cooks up creamy cheese, sage and pancetta pasta.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S]

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. Our coasts have always been an extreme environment to raise a family, but the challenges of parenthood are exacerbated with warming seas - forming earlier than ever before, a hurricane catches a flamingo colony while their chicks are still on the nest. Rain, wind and rising sea levels are a triple threat, but these extraordinary birds have begun to adapt to the new extremes by extending their breeding window and given those who lost their chicks a second chance - meanwhile, a sea otter mum faces a huge winter storm in California and a clownfish on the Great Barrier Reef witnesses her anemone home bleach. However, the clownfish is not ready to give up and sets about reviving it - perhaps most remarkable of all, though, is a little anole lizard that clings on for dear life during a hurricane, surviving as those with the longest toes are the species most able to keep their grip.

programme.title: Octopussy
programme.desc: The 13th entry in the James Bond film series. 007 is asked to investigate the murder of a fellow agent who was clutching a priceless Faberge egg at the time of his death - the trail leads to the mysterious Octopussy, whose travelling circus features a company of gorgeous and athletic women. Bond and Octopussy share a passionate attraction, but 007 soon discovers that the elegant exiled Afghan prince Kamal Khan is working with a mad Soviet officer to hurl mankind into World War III. As Bond tries to stop the nightmarish scheme, his exploits include a tense chase through the streets of India, a deadly brawl on top of a speeding train, and a treacherous mid-air knife fight on an airplane wing.

programme.title: The Chase Celebrity Special
programme.desc: Bradley Walsh hosts as Raj Bisram, Danielle Harold, John Conteh and Roger Black take on a Chaser to try to win thousands of pounds for their chosen charities.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip. Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Zurich to take on The Governess and The Dark Destroyer, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the final city, lose and it's the first flight home. The episode begins with a quiz on Lake Zurich. An eventful race sees the teams take on games in the city involving Einstein, the FIFA Museum and a chocolate factory, before a journey into the Alps for a cable car quiz at the top of a mountain and a James Bond villain's lair.

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Alan is joined at Manor Farm by Dame Eileen Aitkins who talks about her incredible life both on and off screen. Corrie legend William Roache reveals his secrets to a happy life. Plus, the Queen's eldest grandson Peter Phillips invites us to the sporting event of the summer. We also look at the best in drought-resistant plants, and meet a couple of rare breed Guernsey goats.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: For the last time in this series, Fern is back at The Grove Vets to see how they provide treatment and care to their fluffy patients. Andy performs surgery on pooch Pixie's tummy to remove a worrying tumour. Amy investigates a cat's missing kidney via ultrasound, while James removes an infected wart from geriatric Springerdoodle, Coco. Lottie makes an emergency trip to the clinic after accidentally eating some grapes, and two-year-old feline Nico is back for some X-rays on his leg following surgery last year. And we meet the pets and volunteers taking part in a foster care scheme run by Bristol Animal Rescue Centre.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Chef Tom Kerridge is on the road in Italy's mountains, meeting producers who are just as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck, he discovers the secrets behind chestnuts and pasta. In Emilia-Romagna, he heads high into the Apennines to join local producer Adrian at the chestnut harvest. He learns about their importance to the food of this region, as well as seeing the back-breaking work that goes into harvesting on the side of a mountain. Tom cooks a feast to say thank you: a mouth-watering pork loin steak with chestnuts and wild mushrooms. High in the dramatic Dolomites, Tom visits a desmontegada - a festival to mark the changing of the seasons - where he learns about the powerful impact the fresh mountains have on the local cuisine, including the local pasta. With the mountains as inspiration, he cooks up creamy cheese, sage and pancetta pasta.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S,HD]

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. Our coasts have always been an extreme environment to raise a family, but the challenges of parenthood are exacerbated with warming seas - forming earlier than ever before, a hurricane catches a flamingo colony while their chicks are still on the nest. Rain, wind and rising sea levels are a triple threat, but these extraordinary birds have begun to adapt to the new extremes by extending their breeding window and given those who lost their chicks a second chance - meanwhile, a sea otter mum faces a huge winter storm in California and a clownfish on the Great Barrier Reef witnesses her anemone home bleach. However, the clownfish is not ready to give up and sets about reviving it - perhaps most remarkable of all, though, is a little anole lizard that clings on for dear life during a hurricane, surviving as those with the longest toes are the species most able to keep their grip.

programme.title: Octopussy
programme.desc: The 13th entry in the James Bond film series. 007 is asked to investigate the murder of a fellow agent who was clutching a priceless Faberge egg at the time of his death - the trail leads to the mysterious Octopussy, whose travelling circus features a company of gorgeous and athletic women. Bond and Octopussy share a passionate attraction, but 007 soon discovers that the elegant exiled Afghan prince Kamal Khan is working with a mad Soviet officer to hurl mankind into World War III. As Bond tries to stop the nightmarish scheme, his exploits include a tense chase through the streets of India, a deadly brawl on top of a speeding train, and a treacherous mid-air knife fight on an airplane wing.

programme.title: The Chase Celebrity Special
programme.desc: Bradley Walsh hosts as Raj Bisram, Danielle Harold, John Conteh and Roger Black take on a Chaser to try to win thousands of pounds for their chosen charities.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip. Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Zurich to take on The Governess and The Dark Destroyer, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the final city, lose and it's the first flight home. The episode begins with a quiz on Lake Zurich. An eventful race sees the teams take on games in the city involving Einstein, the FIFA Museum and a chocolate factory, before a journey into the Alps for a cable car quiz at the top of a mountain and a James Bond villain's lair.

programme.title: ITV Evening News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world as well as the latest major sports results. [S,HD]

programme.title: ITV News Granada Reports
programme.desc: The latest news and weather from around the North West. [S,HD]

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Cold-adapted animals are struggling in a warming world - high in the peaks of the Indian Himalayas, a snow leopard is forced from his home by a rival male and embarks on a journey lower into the valley where he encounters the human world. Elsewhere, an arctic ground squirrel in Alaska undertakes the coldest migration of any mammal - to do so, he shuts down many of his biological processes. When he awakes, the squirrel must go through puberty again before finding a mate who is only receptive for a single day - the problem is that the warm weather has brought her out a week early and, despite the intention, he is not equipped to mate. Unless they can adapt quickly, their whole species is under threat - meanwhile, a young arctic fox in Svalbard must face her first winter alone and cross more than 2000 miles of semi-frozen ocean to find polar bears on the sea ice there.

programme.title: Van der Valk
programme.desc: When a scientist researching a potential breakthrough in the treatment of cancer is found dead, seemingly assassinated by a professional killer, Van Der Valk and the team have to discover why he was killed and what the possible link is to pharmaceuticals billionaire, Freddie Klink. Realising that the research scientist possibly hid his breakthrough discovery, the team have to figure out where and crack a cryptic code in order to retrieve it. At the same time, they have to field the murderous efforts of other parties equally interested in getting their hands on the new discovery. Is Klink the mastermind behind trying to control any discoveries? Is he possibly even trying to stop a medical breakthrough ever seeing the light of day? Or is there another reason altogether for the killings?

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S,HD]

programme.title: Sunny Nights
programme.desc: The first episode of a comedy-drama series. American siblings Martin and Vicki Marvin have flown across the world with dreams of making their burgeoning spray tan company Tansform a success - it's the fresh start they both desperately need, as Martin hopes that building a successful company is the kind of daring gesture that will win back his estranged wife Joyce while Vicki wants to prove that she can be more than just an impulse-driven underachiever. Arriving in Sydney for a beauty convention, the siblings check into the extremely dodgy-looking Sunny Nights motel and quickly get to work trying to find a retail partner who will stock their spray tan - their plans are disrupted when Martin is rejected by Joyce and is led into a drunken one-night stand with Susi Kamdani, who just happens to be a conwoman. The next morning sees footage of the tryst used by criminal Kash Monroe to blackmail Martin - told he needs to pay to keep the footage private, Martin and Vicki must find ten grand.

programme.title: 25 Years in Afghanistan
programme.desc: Documentary revisiting Mir, whose life audiences followed from childhood through two decades of extraordinary change in the 2021 BAFTA-winning documentary My Childhood, My Country - 20 Years in Afghanistan, adding new footage that charts the five years since the Taliban regained power in 2021.

programme.desc: True-crime documentary series following world-leading forensic scientists as they unlock the forensic secrets of unsolved murders. Dr Angela Gallop reveals how clues in the blood helped solve two terrible crimes including the killing of ten-year-old Damilola Taylor.

Tom cooks a feast to say thank you: a mouth-watering pork loin steak with chestnuts and wild mushrooms. programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S]

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. Our coasts have always been an extreme environment to raise a family, but the challenges of parenthood are exacerbated with warming seas - forming earlier than ever before, a hurricane catches a flamingo colony while their chicks are still on the nest. Rain, wind and rising sea levels are a triple threat, but these extraordinary birds have begun to adapt to the new extremes by extending their breeding window and given those who lost their chicks a second chance - meanwhile, a sea otter mum faces a huge winter storm in California and a clownfish on the Great Barrier Reef witnesses her anemone home bleach. However, the clownfish is not ready to give up and sets about reviving it - perhaps most remarkable of all, though, is a little anole lizard that clings on for dear life during a hurricane, surviving as those with the longest toes are the species most able to keep their grip.

programme.title: Octopussy
programme.desc: The 13th entry in the James Bond film series. 007 is asked to investigate the murder of a fellow agent who was clutching a priceless Faberge egg at the time of his death - the trail leads to the mysterious Octopussy, whose travelling circus features a company of gorgeous and athletic women. Bond and Octopussy share a passionate attraction, but 007 soon discovers that the elegant exiled Afghan prince Kamal Khan is working with a mad Soviet officer to hurl mankind into World War III. As Bond tries to stop the nightmarish scheme, his exploits include a tense chase through the streets of India, a deadly brawl on top of a speeding train, and a treacherous mid-air knife fight on an airplane wing.

programme.title: The Chase Celebrity Special
programme.desc: Bradley Walsh hosts as Raj Bisram, Danielle Harold, John Conteh and Roger Black take on a Chaser to try to win thousands of pounds for their chosen charities.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip. Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Zurich to take on The Governess and The Dark Destroyer, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the final city, lose and it's the first flight home. The episode begins with a quiz on Lake Zurich. An eventful race sees the teams take on games in the city involving Einstein, the FIFA Museum and a chocolate factory, before a journey into the Alps for a cable car quiz at the top of a mountain and a James Bond villain's lair.

programme.title: ITV Evening News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world as well as the latest major sports results. [S]

programme.title: ITV News Granada Reports
programme.desc: The latest news and weather from around the North West. [S]

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Cold-adapted animals are struggling in a warming world - high in the peaks of the Indian Himalayas, a snow leopard is forced from his home by a rival male and embarks on a journey lower into the valley where he encounters the human world. Elsewhere, an arctic ground squirrel in Alaska undertakes the coldest migration of any mammal - to do so, he shuts down many of his biological processes. When he awakes, the squirrel must go through puberty again before finding a mate who is only receptive for a single day - the problem is that the warm weather has brought her out a week early and, despite the intention, he is not equipped to mate. Unless they can adapt quickly, their whole species is under threat - meanwhile, a young arctic fox in Svalbard must face her first winter alone and cross more than 2000 miles of semi-frozen ocean to find polar bears on the sea ice there.

programme.title: Van der Valk
programme.desc: When a scientist researching a potential breakthrough in the treatment of cancer is found dead, seemingly assassinated by a professional killer, Van Der Valk and the team have to discover why he was killed and what the possible link is to pharmaceuticals billionaire, Freddie Klink. Realising that the research scientist possibly hid his breakthrough discovery, the team have to figure out where and crack a cryptic code in order to retrieve it. At the same time, they have to field the murderous efforts of other parties equally interested in getting their hands on the new discovery. Is Klink the mastermind behind trying to control any discoveries? Is he possibly even trying to stop a medical breakthrough ever seeing the light of day? Or is there another reason altogether for the killings?

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S]

programme.title: Sunny Nights
programme.desc: The first episode of a comedy-drama series. American siblings Martin and Vicki Marvin have flown across the world with dreams of making their burgeoning spray tan company Tansform a success - it's the fresh start they both desperately need, as Martin hopes that building a successful company is the kind of daring gesture that will win back his estranged wife Joyce while Vicki wants to prove that she can be more than just an impulse-driven underachiever. Arriving in Sydney for a beauty convention, the siblings check into the extremely dodgy-looking Sunny Nights motel and quickly get to work trying to find a retail partner who will stock their spray tan - their plans are disrupted when Martin is rejected by Joyce and is led into a drunken one-night stand with Susi Kamdani, who just happens to be a conwoman. The next morning sees footage of the tryst used by criminal Kash Monroe to blackmail Martin - told he needs to pay to keep the footage private, Martin and Vicki must find ten grand.

programme.title: 25 Years in Afghanistan
programme.desc: Documentary revisiting Mir, whose life audiences followed from childhood through two decades of extraordinary change in the 2021 BAFTA-winning documentary My Childhood, My Country - 20 Years in Afghanistan, adding new footage that charts the five years since the Taliban regained power in 2021.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: For the last time in this series, Fern is back at The Grove Vets to see how they provide treatment and care to their fluffy patients. Andy performs surgery on pooch Pixie's tummy to remove a worrying tumour. Amy investigates a cat's missing kidney via ultrasound, while James removes an infected wart from geriatric Springerdoodle, Coco. Lottie makes an emergency trip to the clinic after accidentally eating some grapes, and two-year-old feline Nico is back for some X-rays on his leg following surgery last year. And we meet the pets and volunteers taking part in a foster care scheme run by Bristol Animal Rescue Centre.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Chef Tom Kerridge is on the road in Italy's mountains, meeting producers who are just as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck, he discovers the secrets behind chestnuts and pasta. In Emilia-Romagna, he heads high into the Apennines to join local producer Adrian at the chestnut harvest. He learns about their importance to the food of this region, as well as seeing the back-breaking work that goes into harvesting on the side of a mountain. Tom cooks a feast to say thank you: a mouth-watering pork loin steak with chestnuts and wild mushrooms. High in the dramatic Dolomites, Tom visits a desmontegada - a festival to mark the changing of the seasons - where he learns about the powerful impact the fresh mountains have on the local cuisine, including the local pasta. With the mountains as inspiration, he cooks up creamy cheese, sage and pancetta pasta.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. Our coasts have always been an extreme environment to raise a family, but the challenges of parenthood are exacerbated with warming seas - forming earlier than ever before, a hurricane catches a flamingo colony while their chicks are still on the nest. Rain, wind and rising sea levels are a triple threat, but these extraordinary birds have begun to adapt to the new extremes by extending their breeding window and given those who lost their chicks a second chance - meanwhile, a sea otter mum faces a huge winter storm in California and a clownfish on the Great Barrier Reef witnesses her anemone home bleach. However, the clownfish is not ready to give up and sets about reviving it - perhaps most remarkable of all, though, is a little anole lizard that clings on for dear life during a hurricane, surviving as those with the longest toes are the species most able to keep their grip.

programme.title: Octopussy
programme.desc: The 13th entry in the James Bond film series. 007 is asked to investigate the murder of a fellow agent who was clutching a priceless Faberge egg at the time of his death - the trail leads to the mysterious Octopussy, whose travelling circus features a company of gorgeous and athletic women. Bond and Octopussy share a passionate attraction, but 007 soon discovers that the elegant exiled Afghan prince Kamal Khan is working with a mad Soviet officer to hurl mankind into World War III. As Bond tries to stop the nightmarish scheme, his exploits include a tense chase through the streets of India, a deadly brawl on top of a speeding train, and a treacherous mid-air knife fight on an airplane wing.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Chef Tom Kerridge is on the road in Italy's mountains, meeting producers who are just as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck, he discovers the secrets behind chestnuts and pasta. In Emilia-Romagna, he heads high into the Apennines to join local producer Adrian at the chestnut harvest. He learns about their importance to the food of this region, as well as seeing the back-breaking work that goes into harvesting on the side of a mountain. Tom cooks a feast to say thank you: a mouth-watering pork loin steak with chestnuts and wild mushrooms. High in the dramatic Dolomites, Tom visits a desmontegada - a festival to mark the changing of the seasons - where he learns about the powerful impact the fresh mountains have on the local cuisine, including the local pasta. With the mountains as inspiration, he cooks up creamy cheese, sage and pancetta pasta.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S,HD]

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. Our coasts have always been an extreme environment to raise a family, but the challenges of parenthood are exacerbated with warming seas - forming earlier than ever before, a hurricane catches a flamingo colony while their chicks are still on the nest. Rain, wind and rising sea levels are a triple threat, but these extraordinary birds have begun to adapt to the new extremes by extending their breeding window and given those who lost their chicks a second chance - meanwhile, a sea otter mum faces a huge winter storm in California and a clownfish on the Great Barrier Reef witnesses her anemone home bleach. However, the clownfish is not ready to give up and sets about reviving it - perhaps most remarkable of all, though, is a little anole lizard that clings on for dear life during a hurricane, surviving as those with the longest toes are the species most able to keep their grip.

programme.title: Octopussy
programme.desc: The 13th entry in the James Bond film series. 007 is asked to investigate the murder of a fellow agent who was clutching a priceless Faberge egg at the time of his death - the trail leads to the mysterious Octopussy, whose travelling circus features a company of gorgeous and athletic women. Bond and Octopussy share a passionate attraction, but 007 soon discovers that the elegant exiled Afghan prince Kamal Khan is working with a mad Soviet officer to hurl mankind into World War III. As Bond tries to stop the nightmarish scheme, his exploits include a tense chase through the streets of India, a deadly brawl on top of a speeding train, and a treacherous mid-air knife fight on an airplane wing.

programme.title: The Chase Celebrity Special
programme.desc: Bradley Walsh hosts as Raj Bisram, Danielle Harold, John Conteh and Roger Black take on a Chaser to try to win thousands of pounds for their chosen charities.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip. Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Zurich to take on The Governess and The Dark Destroyer, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the final city, lose and it's the first flight home. The episode begins with a quiz on Lake Zurich. An eventful race sees the teams take on games in the city involving Einstein, the FIFA Museum and a chocolate factory, before a journey into the Alps for a cable car quiz at the top of a mountain and a James Bond villain's lair.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Cold-adapted animals are struggling in a warming world - high in the peaks of the Indian Himalayas, a snow leopard is forced from his home by a rival male and embarks on a journey lower into the valley where he encounters the human world. Elsewhere, an arctic ground squirrel in Alaska undertakes the coldest migration of any mammal - to do so, he shuts down many of his biological processes. When he awakes, the squirrel must go through puberty again before finding a mate who is only receptive for a single day - the problem is that the warm weather has brought her out a week early and, despite the intention, he is not equipped to mate. Unless they can adapt quickly, their whole species is under threat - meanwhile, a young arctic fox in Svalbard must face her first winter alone and cross more than 2000 miles of semi-frozen ocean to find polar bears on the sea ice there.

programme.title: Van der Valk
programme.desc: When a scientist researching a potential breakthrough in the treatment of cancer is found dead, seemingly assassinated by a professional killer, Van Der Valk and the team have to discover why he was killed and what the possible link is to pharmaceuticals billionaire, Freddie Klink. Realising that the research scientist possibly hid his breakthrough discovery, the team have to figure out where and crack a cryptic code in order to retrieve it. At the same time, they have to field the murderous efforts of other parties equally interested in getting their hands on the new discovery. Is Klink the mastermind behind trying to control any discoveries? Is he possibly even trying to stop a medical breakthrough ever seeing the light of day? Or is there another reason altogether for the killings?

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip. Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Zurich to take on The Governess and The Dark Destroyer, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the final city, lose and it's the first flight home. The episode begins with a quiz on Lake Zurich. An eventful race sees the teams take on games in the city involving Einstein, the FIFA Museum and a chocolate factory, before a journey into the Alps for a cable car quiz at the top of a mountain and a James Bond villain's lair.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Cold-adapted animals are struggling in a warming world - high in the peaks of the Indian Himalayas, a snow leopard is forced from his home by a rival male and embarks on a journey lower into the valley where he encounters the human world. Elsewhere, an arctic ground squirrel in Alaska undertakes the coldest migration of any mammal - to do so, he shuts down many of his biological processes. When he awakes, the squirrel must go through puberty again before finding a mate who is only receptive for a single day - the problem is that the warm weather has brought her out a week early and, despite the intention, he is not equipped to mate. Unless they can adapt quickly, their whole species is under threat - meanwhile, a young arctic fox in Svalbard must face her first winter alone and cross more than 2000 miles of semi-frozen ocean to find polar bears on the sea ice there.

programme.title: Van der Valk
programme.desc: When a scientist researching a potential breakthrough in the treatment of cancer is found dead, seemingly assassinated by a professional killer, Van Der Valk and the team have to discover why he was killed and what the possible link is to pharmaceuticals billionaire, Freddie Klink. Realising that the research scientist possibly hid his breakthrough discovery, the team have to figure out where and crack a cryptic code in order to retrieve it. At the same time, they have to field the murderous efforts of other parties equally interested in getting their hands on the new discovery. Is Klink the mastermind behind trying to control any discoveries? Is he possibly even trying to stop a medical breakthrough ever seeing the light of day? Or is there another reason altogether for the killings?

programme.title: Sunny Nights
programme.desc: The first episode of a comedy-drama series. American siblings Martin and Vicki Marvin have flown across the world with dreams of making their burgeoning spray tan company Tansform a success - it's the fresh start they both desperately need, as Martin hopes that building a successful company is the kind of daring gesture that will win back his estranged wife Joyce while Vicki wants to prove that she can be more than just an impulse-driven underachiever. Arriving in Sydney for a beauty convention, the siblings check into the extremely dodgy-looking Sunny Nights motel and quickly get to work trying to find a retail partner who will stock their spray tan - their plans are disrupted when Martin is rejected by Joyce and is led into a drunken one-night stand with Susi Kamdani, who just happens to be a conwoman. The next morning sees footage of the tryst used by criminal Kash Monroe to blackmail Martin - told he needs to pay to keep the footage private, Martin and Vicki must find ten grand.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: For the last time in this series, Fern is back at The Grove Vets to see how they provide treatment and care to their fluffy patients. Andy performs surgery on pooch Pixie's tummy to remove a worrying tumour. Amy investigates a cat's missing kidney via ultrasound, while James removes an infected wart from geriatric Springerdoodle, Coco. Lottie makes an emergency trip to the clinic after accidentally eating some grapes, and two-year-old feline Nico is back for some X-rays on his leg following surgery last year. And we meet the pets and volunteers taking part in a foster care scheme run by Bristol Animal Rescue Centre.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Chef Tom Kerridge is on the road in Italy's mountains, meeting producers who are just as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck, he discovers the secrets behind chestnuts and pasta. In Emilia-Romagna, he heads high into the Apennines to join local producer Adrian at the chestnut harvest. He learns about their importance to the food of this region, as well as seeing the back-breaking work that goes into harvesting on the side of a mountain. Tom cooks a feast to say thank you: a mouth-watering pork loin steak with chestnuts and wild mushrooms. High in the dramatic Dolomites, Tom visits a desmontegada - a festival to mark the changing of the seasons - where he learns about the powerful impact the fresh mountains have on the local cuisine, including the local pasta. With the mountains as inspiration, he cooks up creamy cheese, sage and pancetta pasta.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. Our coasts have always been an extreme environment to raise a family, but the challenges of parenthood are exacerbated with warming seas - forming earlier than ever before, a hurricane catches a flamingo colony while their chicks are still on the nest. Rain, wind and rising sea levels are a triple threat, but these extraordinary birds have begun to adapt to the new extremes by extending their breeding window and given those who lost their chicks a second chance - meanwhile, a sea otter mum faces a huge winter storm in California and a clownfish on the Great Barrier Reef witnesses her anemone home bleach. However, the clownfish is not ready to give up and sets about reviving it - perhaps most remarkable of all, though, is a little anole lizard that clings on for dear life during a hurricane, surviving as those with the longest toes are the species most able to keep their grip.

programme.title: Octopussy
programme.desc: The 13th entry in the James Bond film series. 007 is asked to investigate the murder of a fellow agent who was clutching a priceless Faberge egg at the time of his death - the trail leads to the mysterious Octopussy, whose travelling circus features a company of gorgeous and athletic women. Bond and Octopussy share a passionate attraction, but 007 soon discovers that the elegant exiled Afghan prince Kamal Khan is working with a mad Soviet officer to hurl mankind into World War III. As Bond tries to stop the nightmarish scheme, his exploits include a tense chase through the streets of India, a deadly brawl on top of a speeding train, and a treacherous mid-air knife fight on an airplane wing.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Cold-adapted animals are struggling in a warming world - high in the peaks of the Indian Himalayas, a snow leopard is forced from his home by a rival male and embarks on a journey lower into the valley where he encounters the human world. Elsewhere, an arctic ground squirrel in Alaska undertakes the coldest migration of any mammal - to do so, he shuts down many of his biological processes. When he awakes, the squirrel must go through puberty again before finding a mate who is only receptive for a single day - the problem is that the warm weather has brought her out a week early and, despite the intention, he is not equipped to mate. Unless they can adapt quickly, their whole species is under threat - meanwhile, a young arctic fox in Svalbard must face her first winter alone and cross more than 2000 miles of semi-frozen ocean to find polar bears on the sea ice there.

programme.title: Van der Valk
programme.desc: When a scientist researching a potential breakthrough in the treatment of cancer is found dead, seemingly assassinated by a professional killer, Van Der Valk and the team have to discover why he was killed and what the possible link is to pharmaceuticals billionaire, Freddie Klink. Realising that the research scientist possibly hid his breakthrough discovery, the team have to figure out where and crack a cryptic code in order to retrieve it. At the same time, they have to field the murderous efforts of other parties equally interested in getting their hands on the new discovery. Is Klink the mastermind behind trying to control any discoveries? Is he possibly even trying to stop a medical breakthrough ever seeing the light of day? Or is there another reason altogether for the killings?
